column1: # The CROSS-SECTIONAL DRIFT DISPERSION ruler for `-basketdrift`: how much the names of a real
# basket differ in their own long-run drift, once the noise of a finite window is taken out.
# Measured 2026-09-03 from daily Yahoo adjusted closes over 2012-01-04..2026-08-31 (T = 14.6
# years), LOG returns, on the same two groups the basket ruler uses (`basket-2026-09-02.tsv`):
# folio's eight semiconductor names under SMH, and the cache's 26 single names with data from
# 2012.  `scratchpad drift/measure.py`.
# THE DECOMPOSITION.  A name's realized drift over T years is its true drift plus estimation
# noise, and the noise has sd = (the name's idio vol) / sqrt(T) -- so a cross-section of realized
# drifts is dispersed even when every true drift is identical.  `driftSpread` is the observed
# cross-sectional sd; `noiseFloor` is the mean per-name noise sd that T alone generates;
# `trueSpread` is sqrt(max(0, driftSpread^2 - noiseFloor^2)), clamped at 0.
# THE RESULT, AND WHY THE DIAL SHIPS AT 0.  For both groups the observed spread is BELOW the
# noise floor, so `trueSpread` is 0: over this window, among these names, no true drift dispersion
# is detectable at all.  And the groups are selected TODAY -- survivors -- which truncates the
# left tail of realized drift and biases the estimate DOWN.  So 0 is a FLOOR from biased data,
# not a measurement of the world.  The true value needs point-in-time membership including the
# names that left the universe, which no cache here holds; that is the same limitation the basket
# fixture already discloses for `nameD20`, and it is why `-basketdrift` is ungraded.
# WHAT THIS DIAL DOES NOT FIX.  The names' time below peak is not a dispersion miss: the eight's
# COMMON drift is +0.304/yr against the model's +0.144 (beta 1.37 x the Nasdaq recipe's 0.105),
# and that difference is the whole of it.  Dispersion around the right centre widens the spread of
# time-below-peak across names -- which is what the dial is for, and what `nameD20Spread` reads --
# and leaves the MEDIAN where it was.  Raising the centre to the eight's +0.304 would be
# calibrating the model to names selected for having won, so it is not on offer.
# `alphaSpread` / `alphaNoiseFloor` repeat the decomposition on the residual after regressing each
# name on the group index (SMH), which removes the part of the drift spread that is beta times the
# index's own drift.  Same answer.
